evidence.description: The shared singleton uses nonisolated(unsafe) and MainActor.assumeIsolated to instantiate a @MainActor class.

candidates.explanation: The shared singleton instance uses 'nonisolated(unsafe)' and 'MainActor.assumeIsolated' to initialize a class marked with '@MainActor'. This can lead to undefined behavior or crashes if the initialization is accessed from a thread other than the main thread before the actor is fully ready.
candidates.title: Potential Race Condition in Singleton Initialization

evidence.description: A Task with @MainActor is created inside a method already marked @MainActor to update a property.

candidates.explanation: The method 'handleUserProfileUpdate' is marked with @MainActor, but it creates a new Task with @MainActor to update 'isLoggedIn', which is already on the main actor. This adds unnecessary overhead and complexity.
candidates.title: Redundant Task Creation on Main Actor

evidence.description: Notification observer is set to .main queue but uses a Task to call an async method.
Notification observer is set to .main queue but uses a Task to call an async method.
Notification observer is set to .main queue but uses a Task to call an async method.

candidates.explanation: The notification observers are configured to run on the .main queue, but then immediately wrap the handler in a new Task. This is redundant as the handler is already executing on the main thread, and it creates unnecessary asynchronous context switching.
candidates.title: Nested Task in Notification Observer

evidence.description: Hardcoded DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter delays are used to manage animation timing.

candidates.explanation: The use of hardcoded 'asyncAfter' delays (1.0s and 3.0s) for UI animations makes the UI feel unresponsive to actual state changes and can lead to visual glitches if the state changes more rapidly than the delays.
candidates.title: Hardcoded Animation Delays
